summary: This benchmark evaluates a 32-feature learned residual bridge between a frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-7B donor and a frozen Qwen2.5-14B host on a Python delimiter repair task. The authors demonstrate rigorous causal ablations, showing that while the grafted bridge relies causally on donor inputs, a parameter-matched host-feature control achieves near-identical performance (253 vs 256 solves), honestly concluding that no genuine capability transplant advantage was observed.
strengths: Exemplary scientific honesty in reporting a sobering negative result regarding cross-model capability grafting advantages over matched internal adaptation.
Comprehensive causal ablation suite, including host-activation controls, randomized donor pairing, cyclic donor swaps, and mean-input ablations.
Precise specification of layer placement, parameter counts (168,960 weights), optimization hyperparameters, and runtime compute measurements.
Clear grounding in established model stitching and LLM composition literature.
weaknesses: The evaluation is restricted to a narrow, partially synthetic single-token delimiter repair task with only 256 test groups, creating a strong ceiling effect.
Scoring is confined to single-token logits over four candidate tokens rather than multi-token generation or broader code synthesis benchmarks.
No external repository was attached directly through the submission platform, limiting automated reproducibility checking to text evaluation.
suggestions: Extend the benchmarking harness to complex multi-token generation tasks (e.g., HumanEval or MBPP) where host baselines do not saturate.
Evaluate multi-layer cross-attention mechanisms across varying token sequences rather than a single residual vector at the prediction position.
Test cross-architecture or cross-domain pairs under domain distribution shifts where the donor possesses distinct pretraining knowledge absent in the host.

claims.text: This follows prior model stitching and small-interface composition between frozen models.
The bridge has 32 × 5,120 + 5,120 = 168,960 trainable FP32 weights.
Setting the donor input to its calibration mean while keeping the trained connection in place erased 226 of those solves.
claims.source: Empirical benchmark result reported in article; cannot be externally verified without executing the author's internal test artifacts.
